item.title: Deploy Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base for Voice Cloning on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
item.description:
Deploy Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base for Voice Cloning on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

The Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base text-to-speech model is now available for deployment to fully managed, real-time inference endpoints via Amazon SageMaker JumpStart.

🔍 Overview

Qwen3-TTS is a publicly available text-to-speech model family developed by the Qwen team at Alibaba Cloud. The model family supports streaming generation for low-latency, interactive scenarios and uses the Qwen3-TTS-Tokenizer-12Hz speech tokenizer. It covers 10 languages:

  • Chinese
  • English
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • German
  • French
  • Russian
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish
  • Italian

⚙️ Key details

The Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base variant specializes in voice cloning, which reproduces the vocal identity of a specific speaker without retraining.

Model Variant Primary Function
Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base Performs voice cloning from a user-supplied reference audio clip and transcript
Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice Generates speech from a fixed set of predefined speakers

Capabilities of the Base variant include:

  • Rapid Cloning: Captures timbre, pitch, and cadence from only a few seconds of user audio.
  • Cross-lingual Cloning: Captures a voice from a reference in one language and generates speech in another while preserving vocal identity.

🧩 How it works

Amazon SageMaker JumpStart provides the model artifacts and a pre-built serving container, removing the need to write a custom inference handler.

  1. Request: A client sends an HTTP request to the Amazon SageMaker AI endpoint containing target text, base64-encoded reference audio, and the reference audio’s transcript.
  2. Routing: Amazon SageMaker AI routes the request to a vLLM-Omni serving container running on a GPU instance.
  3. Generation: The “talker stage” generates speech tokens from the text and reference voice, and the “code2wav stage” renders them into a waveform.
  4. Output: The container generates 24 kHz audio output, returned to the client in the requested format (such as WAV).

🚀 Availability

Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base is available in Amazon SageMaker JumpStart alongside Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-CustomVoice and Qwen3-ASR-1.7B. Using Amazon SageMaker AI, users can manage infrastructure provisioning, health monitoring, and automatic scaling for the real-time endpoint.

#AmazonSageMaker #Qwen3 #TextToSpeech #VoiceCloning #MachineLearning

Source: Deploying real-time personalized speech with Qwen3-TTS on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Google Introduces Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash-Lite Text-to-Speech Models
item.description:
Google Introduces Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash-Lite Text-to-Speech Models

Google has introduced two new text-to-speech (TTS) models to the Gemini family, expanding voice generation from static presets into a dynamic creative studio for creators, developers, and enterprises.

⚙️ Model Overview

Model Primary Purpose Key Characteristics
Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS Deep creative direction and character design Natural language prompts for new voices; granular control over acting, pacing, and dialect
Gemini 3.8 Flash-Lite TTS High-volume, cost-efficient scale Optimized for dubbing, audio content creation, and expressive voice agents

🧩 Key Capabilities

  • Voice Creation and Customization: Users can create bespoke voices from scratch using natural language prompting to customize role, accent, and characteristics across more than 100 languages and dialects. This includes access to over 2,000 production-ready voices with regional varieties such as Scots English, Quebec French, and Mexican Spanish.
  • Performance Direction: The models allow for line-by-line direction using stage directions or natural script cues. Users can add realistic textures via scripted vocal bursts and backchanneling, such as <laughs>, <sigh>, <gasp>, and interjections like |mhm| or |yeah|.
  • Advanced Audio Production:
    • Long-form generation: Maintains quality and timbre across hours of audio with minimal speaker drift.
    • Native two-speaker scene staging: Directs multi-turn conversations from a single script while keeping voices distinctly separated.
  • Voice Replication: Consistent vocal profiles can be recreated from a 30-second audio sample of a voice the user has the rights to use.

💡 Performance and Benchmarks

Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS holds the #1 overall spot on Hume AI’s Voice Design Benchmark (71.4) and leads in accent modeling (60.8). Both the Flash and Flash-Lite models secured the #1 and #2 spots, respectively, on Hume AI’s Overall Quality Index. Additionally, blind human preference evaluations on Voice Arena placed these models in top positions for several global languages, including Hindi, Vietnamese, Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, and Mexican Spanish.

🛡️ Safety and Transparency

To protect voice talent and ensure transparency, Google has implemented several safeguards:

  • Consent Verification: Voice replication requires a verbal consent recording from the voice owner that matches the reference speaker.
  • Watermarking: Every audio clip generated by Gemini Audio models is watermarked with SynthID, an imperceptible watermark woven into the audio output.
  • Credentials: The system utilizes C2PA credentials to protect developers and vocal talent.

#Gemini #TextToSpeech #GoogleAI #GenerativeAI #AudioAI

Source: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello

item.title: Study Releases Open-Source Text-to-Speech Voices for Kurdish
item.description:
Study Releases Open-Source Text-to-Speech Voices for Kurdish

A recent study has released three Kurdish voices, 35 hours of recorded speech, and a descriptive paper, all available for free download to address the lack of technology capable of reading Kurdish aloud.

🚀 Availability

  • Three Kurdish voices
  • 35 hours of recorded speech
  • A paper describing the work

⚙️ Key details

  • Data Source: The voices were built from three people reading prepared texts.
  • Performance: While the voices sound fluent, they represent the reading styles of the speakers rather than Kurdish as a whole.
  • Technical Issues:
    • A coding fault mishandles long numbers.
    • Test recordings are left unlabeled among training data.
    • A settings file lists equipment that was never used.

💡 Why it matters

  • Kurdish is spoken by millions, but has limited technology for reading text aloud.
  • The use of prepared texts removes much everyday and regional speech, and does not account for major regional and written variations in Kurdish.
  • Compared to English and German, Kurdish has far less linguistic description and dictionary support to help identify wrong pronunciations, meaning software choices can go unchecked.
  • There is a discrepancy between reports, as the download page claims a stronger result than the paper reports and recommends one voice for general use.

#Kurdish #TextToSpeech #OpenSource #AI

Source: Assessing the Reusability of Public Speech Resources for Low-Resource Languages: A Central Kurdish Case Study

item.title: OpenAudio S1-mini: Bringing Emotional Intelligence to Text-to-Speech Technology
item.description:
🎭 OpenAudio S1-mini: Bringing Emotional Intelligence to Text-to-Speech Technology

📝 Summary

Discover OpenAudio S1-mini, a groundbreaking text-to-speech model that supports 13 languages and over 50 emotional markers. This compact 0.5B parameter model delivers near-professional quality voice synthesis with remarkable accuracy. Learn how this open model is changing the accessibility landscape for content creators and developers working with speech technology.

🌐 The Revolution in Multilingual Voice Synthesis

Text-to-speech technology has evolved dramatically over the past decade, but most solutions have struggled with the natural expressiveness that makes human speech so engaging. Enter OpenAudio S1, a breakthrough TTS system that’s redefining what’s possible in the realm of synthetic speech.

The recently released OpenAudio S1-mini—a distilled version of the larger S1 model—has captured attention across the tech community for delivering exceptional speech synthesis capabilities in a remarkably efficient package. With training on more than 2 million hours of audio data spanning multiple languages, this model represents a significant leap forward in making natural-sounding speech synthesis accessible to developers worldwide.

🌍 Breaking Language Barriers with Impressive Multilingual Support

One of the most impressive aspects of OpenAudio S1-mini is its extensive language support. The model currently handles 13 languages:

  • 🇺🇸 English
  • 🇨🇳 Chinese
  • 🇯🇵 Japanese
  • 🇩🇪 German
  • 🇫🇷 French
  • 🇪🇸 Spanish
  • 🇰🇷 Korean
  • 🇦🇪 Arabic
  • 🇷🇺 Russian
  • 🇳🇱 Dutch
  • 🇮🇹 Italian
  • 🇵🇱 Polish
  • 🇵🇹 Portuguese

This multilingual capability makes it an invaluable tool for global applications, content localization, and accessibility improvements across linguistic boundaries. For developers working on international products, this eliminates the need to integrate multiple language-specific TTS solutions.

🎭 Beyond Words: Emotional Intelligence in Synthetic Speech

What truly sets OpenAudio S1-mini apart is its extensive support for emotional and tonal variation—a feature that’s been notoriously difficult to implement in TTS systems. The model supports an impressive array of emotional markers that can transform flat text into expressive speech:

😀 Emotional Spectrum

The S1-mini can express over 50 distinct emotional states, including:

  • 😡 Angry, furious, frustrated
  • 😢 Sad, depressed, painful
  • 😲 Surprised, astonished, excited
  • 😌 Satisfied, relaxed, confident
  • 😰 Anxious, worried, nervous
  • 😄 Delighted, joyful, amused

🔊 Vocal Tone Control

Beyond emotions, the system supports special tone markers:

  • 🏃‍♂️ “in a hurry tone”
  • 📢 “shouting”
  • 😱 “screaming”
  • 🤫 “whispering”
  • 🗣️ “soft tone”

🎭 Special Expression Markers

The model even handles paralinguistic expressions:

  • 😂 “laughing” (Ha,ha,ha)
  • 😏 “chuckling” (Hmm,hmm)
  • 😭 “sobbing” and “crying loudly”
  • 😮‍💨 “sighing”
  • 😰 “panting”

This emotional intelligence layer transforms the TTS experience from merely functional to truly communicative, enabling applications that can convey not just information but also sentiment and context.

🧠 Technical Performance: Small Package, Powerful Results

Despite being significantly smaller than its full-sized counterpart, OpenAudio S1-mini delivers impressive performance metrics that rival much larger models:

📊 Performance Metrics (English, auto-evaluated)

Metric S1 (4B) S1-mini (0.5B)
WER (Word Error Rate) 0.008 0.011
CER (Character Error Rate) 0.004 0.005
Speaker Distance 0.332 0.380

These numbers reveal that S1-mini maintains near-parity with the larger S1 model despite being approximately 8x smaller (0.5B parameters versus 4B). This efficiency is particularly noteworthy because it makes high-quality TTS accessible on more modest hardware configurations.

The implementation of online Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has clearly paid dividends in both models, contributing to their natural-sounding outputs and high accuracy rates.

🚀 Practical Applications and Access

The applications for such a capable TTS system span numerous industries:

  • 🎮 Game developers can create more dynamic NPC interactions
  • 📱 Accessibility tools can provide more natural-sounding assistance
  • 🎬 Content creators can automate voiceovers with appropriate emotional context
  • 📚 Educational platforms can deliver more engaging audio content
  • 🤖 Voice assistants can communicate with greater nuance

OpenAudio S1-mini is released under the CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 license, making it accessible for non-commercial applications while preserving attribution requirements. Developers interested in testing the model can access a demo through the Fish Audio Playground, while the full technical documentation is available on the OpenAudio website and Fish Speech GitHub repository.

💭 The Future of Voice Synthesis

The impressive capabilities of OpenAudio S1-mini highlight how rapidly TTS technology is advancing. As models become more efficient while maintaining high quality, we’re approaching a future where synthetic speech is virtually indistinguishable from human speech—not just in pronunciation accuracy, but in emotional resonance.

What makes this development particularly exciting is the democratization of advanced voice technology. By compressing sophisticated capabilities into a more compact model, OpenAudio is making these tools accessible to a wider range of developers and use cases.

The question now becomes: how will we responsibly integrate increasingly human-like synthetic voices into our digital ecosystem, and what new applications will emerge when emotional expressiveness becomes a standard feature of TTS technology?
